title: Binomial coefficients mod 1e9+7
statement: Answer many queries C(n, r) mod 10⁹+7 (n ≤ 10⁶, up to 2 × 10⁴ queries; C(n, r) = 0 if r > n).
hints: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n − r)!). Division mod a prime p is multiplication by an inverse.
Fermat: a⁻¹ ≡ a^(p−2) (mod p). Precompute all inverse factorials from the last one backwards.

solution.explanation: Precompute factorials mod p, compute inv_fact[N] = fact[N]^(p−2) by fast exponentiation, then inv_fact[i − 1] = inv_fact[i] · i. Each query is then three multiplications. Pascal's triangle is O(n²) memory and too slow for n = 10⁶. This is the workhorse behind every "count the ways, mod 10⁹+7" problem.
solution.python:
def ncr_queries(queries):
    M = 10**9 + 7
    N = max(max(n for n, r in queries), 1); f = [1] * (N + 1)
    for i in range(1, N + 1): f[i] = f[i - 1] * i % M
    inv = [1] * (N + 1); inv[N] = pow(f[N], M - 2, M)
    for i in range(N, 0, -1): inv[i - 1] = inv[i] * i % M
    return [f[n] * inv[r] % M * inv[n - r] % M if 0 <= r <= n else 0 for n, r in queries]
